title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear amounts and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, it's essential to provide the body with sufficient iron and folate. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports the development of the fetus. However, many pregnant women struggle to find recipes rich in iron and folate. In this article, we'll introduce three simple and delicious recipes that combine iron with vitamin C, providing a nutritious and safe meal for pregnant women.

## Nutrient Analysis
Iron and folate are two crucial nutrients for the health of pregnant women and their fetuses. Iron helps prevent anemia, while folate supports the development of the fetus's brain and nervous system. Vitamin C also plays a vital role in enhancing iron absorption.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Vegetable Bowl
* 100g grilled chicken
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, green beans, broccoli)
* 1 lemon
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Grill the chicken with olive oil and seasonings, then serve with cooked white rice and mixed vegetables. Squeeze lemon juice on top to enhance iron absorption.

## Recipe 2: Beef and Vegetable Stir-Fry Bowl
* 100g beef stir-fry
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, green beans, broccoli)
* 1 lemon
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Stir-fry the beef with olive oil and seasonings, then serve with cooked white rice and mixed vegetables. Squeeze lemon juice on top to enhance iron absorption.

## Recipe 3: Vegetarian Red Bean and Vegetable Bowl
* 100g cooked red beans
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, green beans, broccoli)
* 1 lemon
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Cook the red beans with olive oil and seasonings, then serve with cooked white rice and mixed vegetables. Squeeze lemon juice on top to enhance iron absorption.

## Food Safety Notes
During pregnancy, it's essential to prioritize food safety to avoid the risk of food poisoning. Some important notes include:
* Avoid eating raw or undercooked meat
* Avoid eating raw or undercooked fish
* Avoid eating raw or undercooked eggs
* Avoid eating soft cheeses that are not pasteurized
* Avoid eating cold deli meats that are not reheated

## Conclusion
The three recipes above provide a rich source of iron and folate for pregnant women, while ensuring food safety. Pregnant women can refer to our [meal planner](/planner) for more delicious and nutritious recipes. Additionally, they can explore our [prenatal nutrition category](/blog/prenatal-nutrition) for more information on pregnancy nutrition.

## When to Seek Help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about pregnancy nutrition, they should consult their doctor or a registered dietitian. They can provide personalized guidance and support to ensure a healthy pregnancy.

faqs.question: Why are iron and folate important for pregnant women?
faqs.answer: Iron and folate help prevent anemia and support the development of the fetus.

faqs.question: How can I enhance iron absorption?
faqs.answer: Vitamin C helps enhance iron absorption, so pregnant women should consume foods rich in vitamin C, such as lemons, oranges, or bell peppers, along with iron-rich foods.

faqs.question: Can I eat raw or undercooked meat during pregnancy?
faqs.answer: No, pregnant women should avoid eating raw or undercooked meat to avoid the risk of food poisoning.
